desc:
BigCommerce integrations with ERP, shipping and accounting tools stop the copying and re-typing between systems. Ecom Swift LLC connects your store to the tools your business runs on, using official connectors or the API, and tests with real sample orders.

## What are BigCommerce integrations?

A BigCommerce integration is a link that moves data between your store and another system without a person typing it in. Orders flow to your accounting software. Stock levels flow from your ERP to your catalog. Tracking numbers flow back to customers. Marketplace listings and payment tools stay in step with what you actually have.

Some tools offer an official connector you can switch on. Others need a custom link built on the BigCommerce API. Either way, the goal is the same: one source of truth for each piece of data.

## What manual data entry really costs you

When systems do not talk, someone carries the data between them. That person copies orders into a spreadsheet, updates stock in two places and checks shipping labels by eye. It works until the day volume rises, and then it fails in small, expensive ways: an item sells that is no longer in stock, an invoice is missed, a customer is told the wrong status.

Mistakes like these cost refunds and goodwill. They also use time that could go to buying, marketing and customer service.

## How good integrations improve results

An integration saves time first, since repeated tasks run on their own. It also improves accuracy, since the same order data is used everywhere instead of being retyped. Customers notice the effect in faster dispatch and correct stock information.

Reliability matters as much as the connection itself. A sync that fails silently can do more harm than no sync. That is why we agree field mappings with you, set rules for what wins when two systems disagree, and add alerts and retries. The benefit depends on your volume and tools, so we describe what will be automated, not a figure for time saved.

## What a dependable integration includes

- A clear map of which field in one system matches which field in the other.
- The official connector where one exists and suits your case.
- A custom API link where no connector is available.
- Stock sync rules that say which system leads.
- Order status updates in both directions where the tools allow it.
- Customer and product data mapping.
- Email alerts when a sync fails.
- Retry handling for failed syncs.
- Testing with sample orders before real ones flow.
- A written setup guide for your team.

## How we connect your tools

We begin by listing the tools involved and the data that should move between them. For each link we agree the direction, the timing and the rules for conflicts. Then we configure the connector or build the API link, and run test orders from checkout to the other system and back.

The Basic package connects one tool and proves it with a sample order. Standard connects two tools with stock rules, two-way status updates and error alerts. Premium connects up to three tools, builds a custom API link where no connector exists, adds retry handling and finishes with a handover call. Third-party tools carry their own fees, which you pay to their makers.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which system is the master for stock and for prices.
- Prepare a few real order examples, including awkward ones.
- Keep product codes consistent across all systems.
- Ask for alerts to go to a monitored inbox.
- Test refunds and cancellations, not only normal orders.

**Avoid:**
- Syncing every field just because you can.
- Letting two systems edit the same data without a rule.
- Connecting a tool with no way to see errors.
- Running a first sync on the full live catalog without a test.
- Forgetting to tell your team what has been automated.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store owner still copying orders into accounting software, a seller listing on more than one marketplace who needs stock to stay accurate, and a growing business with an ERP that needs its web store connected to it.

## What we need from you

A list of the tools you want connected, who administers each one, and a note on what should move between them. We never need your passwords. For each system, you add us as a user or developer with limited permissions, or you create an API credential that you can switch off later. If a system has no API at all, we tell you early and suggest the nearest practical route.
